title: Context engineering: filling the window with only what matters

videos.script: Everything the model reads has to fit in one window, and everything in it costs something. {{window}} One question, three sources: seventy tokens of instructions, two hundred of sources, and the headers in between. {{sweep}} Ask for more sources and the answer is found no more often. By the second source, all twenty-six were found. What grows is the bill. {{floor}} The floor decides how many sources there are, before any budget does. {{dupes}} Two documents that say the same thing take two places. One of them can go. {{squeeze}} Inside a source, keep the sentences about the question, and the sources get a third shorter. {{place}} Where a source sits matters to real models: the beginning and the end are read best. This course does not measure that, so the lesson says where the evidence comes from. {{pack}} Then all of it together, as one function: floor, duplicates, compression, a budget, and the order. {{compare}} The same answers, a fifth fewer tokens, and more replies faithful to their sources. {{end}} Bigger windows will not make this go away. People fill them.
